summary: A student recounts how their high school's esports team, formed in September 2023, changed their view of what counts as a sport. Through coaching, NASEF membership, guest speakers and competition, they found a role as team analyst and discovered career paths in the gaming industry. The essay argues that scholastic esports builds community, reinforces STEM learning and broadens school sports.
one_line: A student's first-person account of joining a school esports team and finding community, STEM learning and career paths through scholastic esports.
key_facts: The author's high school announced the formation of an esports team in September 2023, and the author was initially skeptical that gaming was a sport.
Mr. Jeremy Feldon, a history teacher with a secret love for gaming, volunteered to coach the esports team.
The school joined the North American Scholastic Esports Federation (NASEF) on October 15, 2023.
NASEF provided a platform to compete and a curriculum that integrated STEM learning with competitive gaming.
Team roles went beyond players to include analysts, shoutcasters, event organizers and social media managers.
The author was an average player but became the team's analyst, studying game footage and opponent strategies.
Esports coordinator Sarah Tan from the local college visited the school on November 8, 2023 to discuss collegiate esports scholarships and professional opportunities.
Colleges scout not only top players but also people skilled in game development, event management and digital content creation.
The school's first interscholastic competition was on December 12, 2023, against neighboring schools, and it was streamed live for the whole school.
For tournaments the team used project management tools and various communication platforms to organize strategies and collaborate.
Mathematics and physics became relevant through game development sessions and calculating the trajectory of in-game projectiles.
Trisha Nguyen, the school's top-ranked player and valedictorian, exemplified combining academic excellence with competitive gaming.
The author began considering college majors aligned with the gaming industry.
